analysis: This PR changes documentation only (docs/provider/direct-mode.md and docs/reference/configuration.md); no executable source or threat-model YAML is in the supplied units, so no concrete regression is demonstrable. Direct-mode auth, bind and token text is unchanged. The text added at direct-mode.md:50-53 says a local GLM qualification load reads its weights for per-file SHA-256 verification, and that this verification is the artifact hash, with no separate passes (`GLM5NextManagedLoad.verifiedArtifactSHA256`). configuration.md head 584-590 repeats that a managed GLM load publishes its own verification in place of the pre/post bracketing passes. It also says F_NOCACHE reads are followed by `PageCache.drop`. configuration.md head 371 adds `DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE` (default `~/.darkbloom/verified-weights.json`): owner-only records of verified weight hashes, each bound to device, inode, size, mtime and ctime of every file, and startup registration reuses a matching record instead of re-hashing. Unverified contract relevant to T-012/T-027/A-004/TB-003: the implementation (`VerifiedWeightHashStore.swift`, `GLM5NextManagedLoad`) is not supplied, so I cannot confirm that a cached hash cannot be reused for modified weights (in-place edit, restored stat fields, hand-edited JSON by the owner-level operator, or a TOCTOU between verification and load). Removal of the bracketing passes may also weaken pre/post-load verification for GLM. The stat tuple and owner-only file do not defend against a root operator, which T-012 already treats as a trust limit. A reviewer with the code should check: file permissions and symlink handling on the store, whether records are keyed by path, aggregate hash and manifest, whether the stat tuple is rechecked at load, and how the reused hash reaches the coordinator's weight-hash check. The `DARKBLOOM_MEMORY_AVAILABILITY` reclaimable change (page cache counted as available) is an availability/admission policy edit with no confidentiality impact (T-029, T-016 only tangentially).
